name: Crunch
summary: A foundational bodyweight core exercise that isolates the rectus abdominis by flexing the spine while keeping the lower back grounded.

setup: Lie supine on a comfortable, flat surface with your knees bent at approximately 90 degrees and your feet flat on the floor, hip-width apart.
Place your fingertips lightly behind your ears or cross your arms over your chest, ensuring your elbows remain flared outward.
Gently draw your ribs down toward your pelvis to establish initial abdominal engagement.
steps: Contract your abdominal muscles to curl your head, neck, and shoulder blades upward off the floor.
Pause and squeeze your abdominals forcefully at the top of the range of motion, keeping your lower back firmly pressed against the floor.
Lower your upper torso under control until your shoulder blades touch the ground, without fully releasing abdominal tension.
instructions.breathing: Exhale forcefully as you curl upward into the peak contraction, and inhale as you return to the starting position.
cues: Shorten the distance between your ribs and your hips.
Keep your lower back glued to the floor.
Look toward the ceiling to keep space between your chin and chest.

common_faults.fault: Yanking on the back of the neck with the hands, causing cervical strain.
common_faults.correction: Keep fingertips lightly touching the temples or cross arms over the chest, maintaining a neutral neck.

common_faults.fault: Lifting the lower back off the floor, turning the movement into a hip-flexor-driven sit-up.
common_faults.correction: Focus solely on curling the shoulder blades off the floor while keeping the lumbar spine anchored.

common_faults.fault: Using momentum to bounce up and down rapidly.
common_faults.correction: Slow the tempo to a two-second ascent and two-second descent with a distinct pause at peak flexion.

precautions: Avoid excessive neck flexion; maintain roughly a fist-sized gap between your chin and sternum.
